name: Chroma
description: Go highlighter derived from Pygments lexers; used by Hugo, Gitea, glamour

host-language.comment: Pure Go library (module github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v2; master is already github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v3).

form-factor.comment: Go library plus the `chroma` CLI (cmd/chroma; usable as a less(1) LESSOPEN preprocessor). An experimental WASM build (cmd/libchromawasm) powers the playground but is not a published module, so `wasm-module` is not tagged.

license.comment: MIT (Copyright 2017 Alec Thomas). The COPYING file also includes the SIL Open Font License 1.1 for the Liberation Mono font embedded in the SVG formatter; pkg.go.dev reports 'MIT, OFL-1.1'.

package.comment: Go module index for the stable v2 line. v3 (alpha) lives at github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v3.

documentation.comment: No dedicated docs site: README plus the pkg.go.dev API reference. An online playground (swapoff.org/chroma/playground) shows languages and styles.

first-release.comment: Repository created 2017-06-07; publicly announced on Hacker News 2017-09-24, around Hugo's switch from Pygments.

latest-version.comment: Latest stable, released 2026-06-17; checked 2026-11-18. v3.0.0-alpha.1 to alpha.5 (latest 2026-07-08) are also tagged. GitHub marks them as 'Latest' releases, but they are alphas under a new module path.

engine-model.comment: Pygments-style RegexLexer: named states of regex rules with push/pop mutators and emitters (ByGroups, Using). The author says Chroma 'very closely adheres to the design of Pygments'.

regex-engine.comment: Uses github.com/dlclark/regexp2, a backtracking .NET-compatible regex engine, rather than Go's RE2-based regexp. Master depends on regexp2/v2 v2.10.1.

embedded-languages.comment: The HTML lexer delegates <script> bodies to the JavaScript lexer and <style> bodies to the CSS lexer via `<using lexer=...>` (Go emitters Using/UsingByGroup). Template lexers (ERB, Django/Jinja, Go templates) also delegate.

language-auto-detection.comment: `lexers.Analyse(text)` picks the highest-scoring lexer (Lexer.AnalyseText; XML lexers can declare <analyse> regex scores). The README warns that very few languages implement content detection, so coverage is weak.

filename-extension-mapping.comment: Lexer Config carries Filenames, AliasFilenames and MimeTypes globs. `lexers.Match(filename)` and MIME-type lookup resolve a lexer.

resumable-line-state.comment: LexerState (Pos, Stack, State) is an exported type for mutators, but there is no documented API to snapshot per-line state and resume tokenising. Tokenise always takes the full text.

incremental-reparsing.comment: Stateless regex lexing over the whole input. There is no edit-aware reparse.

semantic-distinctions.comment: Pure regex state-machine lexer with no syntax tree or locals tracking. Patterns such as `fn name` may emit NameFunction lexically, but there is no structural role analysis.

bundled-languages.comment: Counted from the README's Supported languages table at v2.27.0 (294 lexer names, checked 2026-11-18). The table includes dialect and session variants such as Python 2, Bash Session and the Genshi variants. The README notes that `chroma --list` is authoritative and the table may lag.

grammar-format.comment: Most lexers are XML files in lexers/embedded/. About 21 lexers that need custom logic are written in Go (e.g. go, markdown, php, raku, svelte, caddyfile, genshi).

grammar-ecosystem-compatibility.comment: Build-time conversion only: `_tools/pygments2chroma_xml.py` turns Pygments lexers into Chroma XML, and Pygments styles were converted with `_tools/style.py`. Pygments lexers cannot be loaded at runtime, and complex lexers need manual ports.

runtime-grammar-loading.comment: `NewXMLLexer(fs.FS, path)` loads an XML lexer at runtime, `MustNewLexer` builds one from Go rules, and `LexerRegistry.Register` / `lexers.Register` adds or replaces a lexer by name.

lazy-grammar-loading.comment: Partly lazy. All embedded XML lexers are registered at package init (config, filename globs and analyser regexes are parsed eagerly). Their rules are decoded only on first use through a fetchRulesFunc closure. All lexers are compiled into the binary via go:embed.

grammar-accuracy.comment: Judgement call. Lexers are hand-maintained Pygments derivatives that don't track an upstream grammar. Mainstream-language gaps are still being fixed in 2024–2026 (TypeScript string-literal generics fixed in v2.15.0; Rust raw identifiers in declarations merged 2026-10-16). The README admits fewer lexers than Pygments and omits some advanced Pygments features.

bundled-themes.comment: 77 XML style files in styles/ at v2.27.0, checked 2026-11-18 (master has 83). Includes all Pygments styles plus Catppuccin, Tokyo Night, Rose Pine, Kanagawa, GitHub (dark), etc.

theme-format.comment: Styles are XML files using Pygments style-entry syntax (e.g. 'bold #f00 bg:#000'). Styles can also be built in Go via NewStyle/StyleBuilder and registered with styles.Register.

token-classification.comment: Closed Pygments-derived TokenType set (e.g. NameFunction, CommentSpecial) with parent inheritance for styling.

css-class-output.comment: html.WithClasses(true) plus ClassPrefix and Formatter.WriteCSS to generate the stylesheet. Inline styles are the default.

multi-theme-output.comment: Via class-based HTML plus WithModeClasses(true). WriteCSS scopes rules as `.chroma.<mode>`, and the documented approach is to call WriteCSS once per style (e.g. a light style and its dark Counterpart), concatenate the CSS, and switch the mode class at runtime. There is no CSS-variable mechanism.

public-token-api.comment: Lexer.Tokenise returns an Iterator over Token{Type, Value}. Helpers include chroma.Tokenise (→ []Token), Iterator.Tokens(), Stdlib() Go iterators, Coalesce and SplitTokensIntoLines. v3 replaces Iterator with iter.Seq[Token].

ir-kinds.comment: Flat (TokenType, Value) stream. The built-in `json` formatter writes it as a JSON array of {"type", "value"} objects. A `tokens` formatter dumps a Go-syntax token listing for debugging.

serializable-ir.comment: Token has json struct tags and TokenType implements text marshalling. The registered `json` formatter emits the token list as JSON. It is not described in the README, but it is part of the public formatter registry.

theme-resolved-tokens.comment: Tokens carry only a TokenType. Style.Get(tokenType) returns a resolved StyleEntry (colour, bold, italic, …), but no API emits tokens with styles attached. Formatters do the join internally.

source-offsets-in-ir.comment: Token struct is only {Type, Value}. Offsets have to be reconstructed by summing value lengths.

custom-formatter-api.comment: Implement chroma.Formatter (Format(w, style, iterator)) or use chroma.FormatterFunc, and register it with formatters.Register.

line-transforms-decorations.comment: Limited to HighlightLines(ranges) in the HTML formatter, plus linkable line-number anchors. There are no diff/focus markers, inline annotations, or per-line hooks. WithPreWrapper only wraps the whole block.

output-formats.comment: v2.27.0 formatters are html, svg (embedded Liberation Mono font), terminal/terminal8/terminal16, terminal256, true-colour terminal, json, tokens and noop. Master (v3 alpha) adds a mIRC formatter, which is not yet in a stable release.

line-numbers.comment: HTML only: WithLineNumbers, LineNumbersInTable, WithLinkableLineNumbers and BaseLineNumber.

streaming-output.comment: Tokens come from a lazy iterator and formatters write to an io.Writer, but Tokenise needs the complete input string. The HTML formatter collects all tokens before writing, because line-number width depends on the total line count. There is no documented incremental-input API.

terminal-ready.comment: Built-in 8/16/256-colour and true-colour terminal formatters, and a CLI that works as a less(1) preprocessor.

native-dependencies.comment: Pure Go: the only runtime dependency is dlclark/regexp2 (pure Go). No cgo.

runs-in-browser.comment: Via the experimental libchromawasm build, which exposes a global JS `highlight(source, lexer, style, classes)` returning HTML. The production playground compiles it to WASM and runs it client-side. There is no published npm package.

wasm-build.comment: In-repo cmd/libchromawasm is documented as an 'experimental WASM library intended for TinyGo'. It is built from source and not distributed as a prebuilt artifact.

synchronous-api.comment: Plain blocking Go calls (Tokenise, Format, quick.Highlight). No async initialisation.

bindings-ports.comment: No official bindings. The only wrapper found is chroma-highlight, a tiny third-party Node.js package (3 stars, bundles chroma v2.4.0) that shells out to the chroma binary, so it doesn't count as well-known. Chroma is itself a Go port of Pygments.

core-package-size.comment: Not comparable: Go modules are compiled into the consumer's binary. Neither pkg.go.dev nor the Go proxy reports an installed size, and binary contribution depends on linked lexers (all are go:embed'ed).

throughput-tier.comment: No independent or reproducible cross-engine benchmark including Chroma was found. Claims of being much faster than Pygments mostly reflect avoiding the pygmentize process spawn in Hugo, as the author notes.

initialization-cost.comment: No time-to-first-highlight measurement was found. Package init registers all ~290 lexer configs (rules are deferred to first use), but the cost is unmeasured.

monthly-downloads.comment: The Go module ecosystem publishes no download counts. As a proxy, pkg.go.dev shows v2 imported by 593 packages (checked 2026-11-18).

last-release.comment: v2.27.0, the latest stable release. v3.0.0-alpha.5 followed on 2026-07-08 but is an alpha.

maintenance-status.comment: Last push 2026-11-18, only 9 open issues, and community lexer PRs merged regularly (e.g. #1373 on 2026-10-16). v3 is in alpha alongside the v2 line.

documentation-quality.comment: Solid README (quick start, language identification, formatter and HTML options, styles, CLI, lexer testing) plus a pkg.go.dev API reference and an online playground and style gallery. There is no guides site or migration notes, and some features (e.g. the json formatter) are documented only in code.

notable-users.value: Hugo, Gitea, glamour (Charm's Markdown renderer behind Glow), moor pager
notable-users.comment: Hugo and Gitea require chroma/v2 v2.27.0, and glamour requires v2.14.0 (checked 2026-11-18). The README lists moor and f4.

bus-factor.comment: Personal repository of Alec Thomas, who reviews and merges all PRs. Many lexers come from community contributors, but there is no maintainer team or organisation.
